findings.claim: The new test asserts the link path is absent from the message via strings.Contains(uninstall.Message, s.files[1]). If s.files[0] is a prefix of or shares a substring with s.files[1], or the message embeds a shared directory, the check is fine; but the assertion combines the Partial status and the absence check in one condition, so a failure message cannot tell which condition failed. Minor diagnostic weakness only.

evidence: The change in removeOwnerRules splits dedup and removal into two passes, so same-file detection via os.Stat runs while every file still exists; this matches the stated fix.
handled.has is only called in the first loop, before any removal, so the dangling-link case no longer reaches it.
The unique slice mirrors handled exactly, so the second loop removes each distinct path once and reports it once; behavior for the non-alias case is unchanged.
The sameFiles comment rewrap preserves its meaning and is comment-only.
